2524.body:
A stopped pusher must not leave its work running, and no pusher, or launcher of one, may join the tree without the same guarantee.

A shell does not forward TERM, INT or HUP to a foreground child, so a stopped pusher exited and its reparented subtree kept running (2026-10-20: six survivors, aged 26 to 62 minutes, on a box at load 77 on eight cores).

**The fix.** `tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh`'s `pr_exit_trap [<command>]` sets one EXIT trap: `<command>`, then `pr_reap`, then `$PR_AFTER_REAP`. Each push or child runs asynchronously and the shell `wait`s on it, so TERM, INT and HUP all interrupt the wait and run the trap. `pr_reap` walks `pgrep -P` from `$$`, TERMs each numeric pid it returned (never a pattern or a group), and KILLs what outlives a 2 s grace. A runner whose child is itself a runner names it `PR_REAP_LEAD`; `pr_reap` TERMs the lead alone first and waits up to `PR_REAP_LEAD_TENTHS` for it to stop its own tree.

Seams closed: the runners `open_pr.sh`, `update_pr.sh`, `handoff_push.sh`, `remerge_main.sh` and `tools/pr/app_push.sh` (its prepr and its own `git push`; `MINT_TRAP=caller` keeps `app_mint.sh`'s traps off the reap); `merge_train.py` (`Train._run` TERMs its tool, never a bare SIGKILL, and `stop_on_signal()` makes a TERM or HUP unwind); `train.sh`, with `merge_train.py` as its lead; `cloud_relay.sh`, with `update_pr.sh` as its lead, launched for the stub and the production route from one backgrounded line (`788a882d7`), which clears the `a01627177715` review's mutation-vacuous block.

Part of #2502, which stays open (`## Forward-carry`).

## Head

`d80da8662c1fdfca0f9f391c04da3b0ecf20c24c` merges main `86425b9` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`e7fc65845c2609b5e2ce7096362460aa53e85b32` merges the authored code head `a0cb0cdd7f2d3955f06dbb65946257a938d633a3` and then merges origin/main `4d407a35f` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`aeb95d4e7cd89bcacab4da92eafb34079f5cc5a4` merges the authored code head `a0cb0cdd7f2d3955f06dbb65946257a938d633a3` and then merges origin/main `4d407a35f` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`a0cb0cdd7f2d3955f06dbb65946257a938d633a3` merges origin/main `50808a755ce300fac4b19b7cfe7f89c795b8387b` (#2580, R10-FLOW-RELAY-HOLD) into the previous PR head `e62be31de2c3d80217d6d855b59f7d27f5392826`, whose parents are `c3bafaf88` and origin/main `a9db47846`; the authored code head `2d5d6be11` is reached through `c3bafaf88`. Everything below was measured at `a0cb0cdd7` unless a line names another commit.

**Conflict resolution, `tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh`.** One hunk, `handoff_arm()`'s `local` line: #2580 adds `held_prs`, this PR adds `upd`. Resolved as the union, `... nonce urc held_prs upd`; no other line conflicted.
- Order in `handoff_arm()`: the contained test (`git merge-base --is-ancestor "$hs" "$head" && continue`), then #2580's hold (`HELD #$pr $hs; continue`), then the failed-update ledger, then the single launch (`"${upd[@]}" ... &`, `PR_REAP_LEAD=$!`). A held PR `continue`s before the launch, so the relay never runs `update_pr.sh` on it.
- That order is pinned: moving the hold line to just after `PR_REAP_LEAD=$!; wait ...` reds 3 of 192 arms (`a held PR whose handoff is ahead is not updated`, `a held PR whose handoff tip moved is still not updated`, `a hold outranks a recorded failed update: still HELD`). #2580's own ordering mutants `cloud_relay-8` and `cloud_relay-9` are killed below.
- No revert of either side: `git diff --stat 50808a755...HEAD` prints `13 files changed, 904 insertions(+), 83 deletions(-)`, the same as at `2d5d6be11`; #2580's hold arms all pass in the merged self-test (192 checks, 84 before #2580).

## Mutation proof

**The review's block, failing test first and fixed.** `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_pusher_reap_launch_mutants.sh` (sha1 `5a4a1925`, unchanged since `db0d88377`) applies each mutant exact-once in a fresh detached worktree and runs the named self-tests:
- At `a01627177715` (the blocked head), `F-CR-ELSEFG` and `F-CR-ELSELEAD` each print `MUTANT F-CR-…: CR rc=0 cloud_relay self-test: 83 checks, 0 failed`, re-run this round (`… a01627177 M0 F-CR-ELSEFG F-CR-ELSELEAD`; M0 there: CR 83/0, TR ok, PA 90/0, AP 186/0, MT 200/0). The block is reproduced.
- At `af7eb2d9a` (the production-route arm, the split launch unchanged), both are killed:
  - `MUTANT F-CR-ELSEFG: CR rc=1 cloud_relay self-test: 84 checks, 1 failed` / `FAIL with no stub, the relay runs update_pr.sh beside it as the lead, asynchronously: a TERM ends it in that order (rc=1, want 0)`
  - `MUTANT F-CR-ELSELEAD: CR rc=1 cloud_relay self-test: 84 checks, 1 failed` / `FAIL with no stub, the relay runs update_pr.sh beside it as the lead, asynchronously: a TERM ends it in that order (rc=1, want 0)`
- At this head, `788a882d7` removed the split line, so `F-CR-ELSEFG` prints `NOT APPLIED at 2d5d6be11` (its anchor occurs 0 times); its successors on the one launch line are killed: `CR-FG` (CR rc=1, `$!: unbound variable` under `set -u`, no summary line) and `CR-FG-BOUND` (`84 checks, 4 failed`, among them the production-route arm). `F-CR-ELSELEAD` still applies and is killed: `cloud_relay self-test: 84 checks, 1 failed` / `FAIL with no stub, the relay runs update_pr.sh beside it as the lead, asynchronously: a TERM ends it in that order (rc=1, want 0)`.

**The sweep at this head**, `bash dev/audit/harnesses/r10_pusher_reap_launch_mutants.sh 2d5d6be11` (every row):

| row | mutant | result at `2d5d6be11` |
|---|---|---|
| M0 | none | CR `84 checks, 0 failed`; TR `ok`; PA `93 checks, 0 failed`; AP `197 checks, 0 failed`; MT `221 checks, 0 failed` |
| CR-FG | relay update launch in the foreground | CR rc=1, no summary line (`$!` unbound under `set -u`) |
| CR-FG-BOUND | the same, `$!` kept bound | CR `84 checks, 4 failed`, including `FAIL with no stub, the relay runs update_pr.sh beside it as the lead, asynchronously: a TERM ends it in that order` |
| CR-LEADNAME | the launch not named `PR_REAP_LEAD` | CR `84 checks, 2 failed`, the stub lead arm and the production-route arm |
| CR-PRODPATH | default command → `update_pr.missing` | CR `84 checks, 1 failed`, the production-route arm alone |
| F-CR-ELSEFG | the review's split-line mutant | `NOT APPLIED at 2d5d6be11` (anchor occurs 0 times); killed at `af7eb2d9a`, above |
| F-CR-ELSELEAD | the production route not named the lead | CR `84 checks, 1 failed`, the production-route arm |
| TR-FG | train.sh launch in the foreground | TR `REFUSE: self-test: the stubbed --ignore-red run did not succeed` |
| TR-LEAD | train.sh lead renamed | TR `REFUSE: … a TERMed train did not stop merge_train.py first (alive 0, marks 'G early ', pidfile removed)` |
| TR-RC | `wait "$PR_REAP_LEAD" \|\| rc=$?` → `\|\| :` | TR `REFUSE: … a child exiting 3 left train.sh rc 0, state/rc '0', log 'TRAIN_RC=0'` |
| OP-FG1 | open_pr's first push in the foreground | PA rc=124 (the 900 s timeout) with 9 arms already failed, among them `open_pr: INT reaps the tree too …` and both census arms |
| OP-FG2 | open_pr's second push in the foreground | PA `93 checks, 3 failed`: both census arms and `mutants mut:oplock and mut:unpushed …` |
| UP-FG | update_pr's push in the foreground | PA rc=124 with 7 arms already failed, among them `update_pr: INT reaps the tree too …`, `update_pr: after the stop the lock is free …` and both census arms |
| HP-FG | handoff_push's push in the foreground | PA `93 checks, 3 failed`: `handoff_push: INT reaps the tree too …` and both census arms |
| RM-FG | remerge_main's push in the foreground | PA `93 checks, 3 failed`: `remerge_main: INT reaps the tree too …` and both census arms |
| AP-FG | app_push's prepr in the foreground | AP `197 checks, 2 failed`: `app_push INTed mid-prepr ends within 4 s, not behind prepr (got 'alive', want 'gone')`, `and leaves none of prepr's tree alive (got '3', want '0')` |
| AP-PUSHFG | app_push's own `git push` in the foreground | AP `197 checks, 16 failed`, led by `app_push INTed mid-push, after the mint, ends within 4 s (got 'alive', want 'gone')` |
| AP-MINTTRAP | `MINT_TRAP=caller` commented out | AP `197 checks, 2 failed`: `and leaves none of the push's tree alive (got '3', want '0')`, TERM and INT arms |
| MT-KILL | `Train._run`'s `p.terminate()` → `p.kill()` | MT `221 checks, 1 failed`: `a TERMed train exits 143 and leaves none of its tool's tree alive (R10-PUSHER-REAP)` |

Every applicable row turns its self-test red, and M0 is green. TR-EXEC (train.sh's `exec ` deleted) stays unpinned: equivalent on bash 5.2 (the previous review measured it), kept for macOS bash 3.2.

## Null control

M0 is green on all five self-tests, so each red above is its mutant's. `CR-PRODPATH` (the default command pointed at a missing file) reds only the production-route arm, so that arm alone runs `bash "$HERE/update_pr.sh"`. merge_train's stop arm has a null control (no `stop_on_signal`, tree survives, `left == 3`) that passes, so the arm can see the defect. An unrelated sleeper survives every TERM arm in pr_args (`open_pr: the null control -- an unrelated sleeper survives`).

## Figures

All at `a0cb0cdd7`, origin/main `50808a755`, `PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1`.

**Self-tests:**

| command | result |
|---|---|
| `bash tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh --self-test` | `cloud_relay self-test: 192 checks, 0 failed` |
| `bash tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh --self-test` | `pr_args self-test: 93 checks, 0 failed` |
| `bash tools/audit/seat/train.sh --self-test` | `train.sh self-test: ok (5 refusals shown, root and options reach the child, no unasked flag, the child's exit is the train's, a stop reaps the tree, merge_train.py first)` |
| `bash tools/pr/app_push.sh --self-test` | `app_push self-test: 197 checks, 0 failed` |
| `bash tools/audit/seat/handoff_push.sh --self-test` | `delivery_row self-test: 5 checks, 0 failed`; `handoff_push self-test: 2 checks, 0 failed` |
| `python3 tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py --self-test` | `merge_train self-test: 221 checks, 0 failed` |

**Launch-mutant harness, CR rows** (`bash dev/audit/harnesses/r10_pusher_reap_launch_mutants.sh HEAD M0 CR-FG CR-FG-BOUND CR-LEADNAME CR-PRODPATH F-CR-ELSEFG F-CR-ELSELEAD`):
- M0: CR `192 checks, 0 failed`; TR ok; PA 93/0; AP 197/0; MT 221/0.
- CR-FG: rc=1, no summary. CR-FG-BOUND: 192/4. CR-LEADNAME: 192/2. CR-PRODPATH: 192/1, the production-route arm alone. F-CR-ELSEFG: NOT APPLIED (its anchor, the split launch, is gone since `788a882d7`). F-CR-ELSELEAD: 192/1.

**#2580's hold mutants** (`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py cloud_relay-1 … cloud_relay-11`): all 11 KILLED, `RESULT survivors=0` (failed arms 1 via a dead stub, 36, 49, 2, 3, 18, 2, 1, 1, 27, 1).

**Gate and ratchet.**
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`; no `*_budgets.json` in the diff.
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff origin/main`: `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out`.
- `ci_predict.py --base origin/main`: `no closures or fast red predicted against 50808a755ce3`. `pr_args.sh --pushers HEAD`: 18 ok, none other. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exited 0.
- Rule 3/4: `git diff --name-only 50808a755...HEAD | grep -E 'VERSION|manifest|RELEASE_NOTES|claimed_drift'` printed nothing, rc 1.
- Not re-run here: the scoped `tests/run.sh` gate, `score.py`, `tmp_paths.py`, `throwaway_git.py`, `policy_lint.mjs`. This container has Python 3.11, on which entities.py fails to parse (a 3.12 f-string), as recorded at `2d5d6be11` where the 3.14 gate passed (`ALL 2397 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`, `5 TEST SCRIPT(S) PASSED`). The merge adds only #2580's files to this diff's base; CI's run on `a0cb0cdd7` is that gate.

## Red checks

From the check-runs API, as recorded:
- `e62be31de` (41 runs): `nightly-status` failure only; `pr-contract`, `closures`, `fast (3.14)`, `mutation`, `instrument-self-tests`, `coverage` success.
- `f99ac55b4` (41 runs) and `a01627177715` (49 runs): `nightly-status` failure only.
- Earlier: `6fd073c9` `PR contract` failed twice (`CodeQL`, `Governance`, `Tests` cancelled by `cancel-superseded`); `50571afa` and `c071fa5f` `PR contract` failed twice each, and `nightly-status`; `9629ae17` `nightly-status`.
- `a0cb0cdd7` has no CI yet; the orchestrator's push is its first run.

Answers:
- `pr-contract` (`6fd073c9`, `50571afa`, `c071fa5f`): the body, not the code — carry_audit refused unrouted items. The cheaper detector, `carry_audit.py check --body`, runs offline in seconds and is run on every body since. The trigger is named; its analysis is `root-cause.md`'s seat.
- `nightly-status` (every head from `50571afa`): it grades main's last scheduled run, which this diff (`tools/` scripts, one harness, `tests/closures.json`, one delivery row) does not reach. No cheaper detector applies to a red this branch did not cause.

## Forward-carry

- #2502's SIGKILL clause ("a TERM, INT, HUP or SIGKILL of a running update must not free the branch lock while its push still runs"): this PR meets TERM, INT and HUP, not SIGKILL — a SIGKILLed run runs no trap, and its lock holder exits within 2 s of losing its parent (`# mut:watch`) while its push may still run. Owed: the holder keeps the lock until the run's former tree is gone, by a drain that waits on a condition, never a fixed window, and passes in a container whose PID 1 reaps late. #2502 stays open; keep `resume.stage` at `in-progress` past #2524's merge. Carry: R10-UPDATE-PR-SIGNALS (`dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json`)
- The roster's Revision-12 self-test isolation ("every self-test runs under a timeout in its own process group, reaped on exit") is not built here: it reaches files outside this group, and a process-group kill is a design question against `pr_kill`'s never-a-group rule. Carry: R10-UPDATE-PR-SIGNALS (`dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json`)

## Friction

2528.body:
prepr's `closures` step (6b) default-skips off Linux, since CI's required `closures` context and
`closures-autofix` own the check, with `PREPR_RECORD_CLOSURES=1` as the opt-in for a lane that needs a
first-green head. The recorder also dies with the prepr. Step 6b runs `closures_line` as a job the prepr
`wait`s on (`closures_step`), and a `$$` watchdog reaps the recorder's process group. Linux is unchanged.
The policy half is `dev/governance/rules/gate-scoping.md` and its two generated copies.

This round changes no code. The review's block was carry-missing: the sibling seams (prepr's
foreground heavy steps 3 to 3h) were routed to `#201`, whose carry file held no entry. They are now
carried to the live roster group R10-FLOW-JIDOKA, which owns `tools/pr/prepr.sh`, and its brief cites
#2528 on the roster ref (`## Figures`). The three round-1 items the review found unrouted are settled
under `## Forward-carry`.

## Head

`e3bee54ebc8fa49390590d9e98f0d5d3525a7061` merges main `50808a7` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`2af78ed5959f39dbe1e2bdee2efa0298ee198312` merges the authored code head `20d129b11e3dc3880e1c9cb2fe3ce0d6b9345370` and then merges origin/main `8a94ffd03` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

`20d129b11e3dc3880e1c9cb2fe3ce0d6b9345370`: the previous head `1723d8743619f397bcf9e04a219e1a581f4a736c` plus one merge of
origin/main `752f697cc` (read 2026-10-22T17:03:52Z), never a rebase; it merged without conflict. The merge base is
`752f697cc`. No code changed this round. `tools/pr/prepr.sh` at this head is blob `a0edc03ab`; main's own
changes to it came in with the merge. Every figure below is at `20d129b11` over base `752f697cc`.

## Mutation proof

Rule: each mutant is a detached worktree at `bb53ba321` with one patch to `tools/pr/prepr.sh`, applied with

comments.body:
Fix review: blocked b18052f664039d36da73ef745a2a8423f82d2c46 vacuous-test: the recorder-reap arm runs closures_line outside a command substitution and without prepr's top-level TERM trap, so deleting the watchdog or the traps leaves it green while production orphans or hangs the recorder

Round 1 (first review of this head). Measured head b18052f664039d36da73ef745a2a8423f82d2c46; it was still the PR head when this was written. Code head 7eee5b39e is byte-identical to it on all five PR files, so the body's measurement at 7eee5b39e carries. Main moved to 5d433771a. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <head>` exits 0 (tree f4b575467), so the merge is clean and no absorb is owed. `fix-review.md` is unchanged on main since the merge base; only orchestrator.md moved.

## Blocking: the second arm (the recorder dies with the prepr) is not pinned

The reap block has two mechanisms: the TERM/INT traps and the `$$` watchdog. The self-test arm "a TERM to the prepr leaves no recorder running behind it" drives `closures_line` directly in `drv.sh`. That is not inside `$(...)`, and the driver evals prepr only up to `rc=0`, so it never sets the slot block's top-level `trap 'exit 143' TERM` (prepr.sh:2683/2692). Production runs `CLOSURES_LINE=$(closures_line "$BASE")` (2922) after that trap is set. So the arm reproduces neither production case.

Step-1 mutants, each a copy of the head's prepr.sh run with `--self-test` under /etc/profile.d/hpo-toolchain.sh (Python 3.14). The head gives 321 passed, 0 failed. M0 (an unmodified copy) gives 320 passed, 1 failed: `a change to prepr.sh owes the self-test`, which is the runner's own failure and is in every row below.
RESULT M1 (delete `return 1` in closures_records_here): 317/4. Killed by the three off-Linux arms (matches the body).
RESULT M2 (delete the PREPR_RECORD_CLOSURES override): 318/3. Killed by the two opt-in arms (matches the body).
RESULT M3setm (delete `set -m`): 319/2. Killed by the reap arm.
RESULT M3trap (delete both `trap 'reap_recorder; ...'` lines): 320/1. SURVIVES. Nothing beyond M0 fails.
RESULT M3wd2 (watchdog body replaced by `( : ) & wpid=$!`): 320/1. SURVIVES. A cruder M3wd that deleted the watchdog line outright failed 6 recording arms through an unset `$wpid`, but the reap arm stayed green.
The body's M3 deletes both mechanisms at once, which hides that each passes alone.

A production-shaped probe (ev/probe.sh) closes that gap. It evals prepr up to `rc=0`, sets the slot block's traps, and calls `X=$(closures_line <base>)` on a clone whose diff touches tests/wood_advisor.py. A sleeper stands in for the recorder, under `setsid`. Each line is the recorder, and the prepr, still alive 5 s after the signal:
RESULT head  KILL->prepr: prepr gone, recorder reaped | base 3688cf2: recorder ORPHANED (the finding's case; the watchdog fixes it)
RESULT head  TERM->pgrp / HUP->pgrp: reaped | base: reaped
RESULT head  TERM->prepr alone: prepr AND recorder alive. The prepr's own trap defers until the recorder finishes (ev/probe-term-deferral.txt: rc 143 at +15 s for a 15 s recorder). Base is the same.
RESULT M3wd/M3wd2 KILL->prepr: recorder ORPHANED. The self-test stays green.
RESULT M3trap TERM->pgrp: prepr AND recorder stay alive. The watchdog subshell holds the `$(...)` pipe open while it waits on `$$`, and `$$` waits on that pipe. This is a hang the traps prevent. The self-test stays green.

So each mechanism is load-bearing in production, and neither is pinned. Also, the arm's name, the code comment at prepr.sh:556-561 ("a TERM to the prepr alone ... still ends the closure work") and the body's "a TERM/INT trap reaps that group" all state a case that the head does not deliver in production. A TERM to the prepr alone is deferred by its own trap, and the recorder runs to completion. What the head delivers is: KILL to the prepr (the watchdog), and TERM or HUP to the process group (the traps). To unblock: drive the arm through `$(closures_line ...)` with prepr's top-level traps installed, and give each mechanism its own arm (KILL the prepr; TERM its group). Then either make a TERM to the prepr alone end the work, or correct the comment, the arm's name and the body to the cases it does cover.

## The rest, which held
- Off-Linux default and opt-in: M1 and M2 kill exactly the arms the body names. The `full` and `skip` lines are pinned byte-identical. Linux behaviour is unchanged (the null-control arm is green at the head).
- Class: tools/pr/prepr.sh has one recorder launch (line 569) and one platform predicate, so the class is one seam. No other seam returned.
- Finder's harness (step 9): the reopened group has no committed harness. Its evidence is the owner ruling plus the roster resume note's 6b-outcome count (108 ok, 13 skip, 3 REFUSE), which is out of tree. I built no instrument of my own beyond ev/probe.sh, which is mine, not the finder's. The body does not carry the roster note's "recommendation on record" (force PREPR_RECORD_CLOSURES=1 on diffs touching tests/closures.json, tests/closure.py or an INERT read). That is not an owner ruling, so it is not a block, but it is undispositioned.
- Figures re-derived at the head (ev/cheap-checks.txt):
  - `RULES-SYNC ok`, and 0 conflict markers in both generated copies.
  - `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out.`, with scope.run = tests/entities.py.
  - `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`, and `claims hygiene: 3688cf2 ok`.
  - The self-test gives 321 passed, 0 failed.
  - VERSION, the manifest, RELEASE_NOTES and tests/golden are untouched. No claim file moved.
- CI at this head (check-runs API, ev/check-runs.tsv): every run concluded. The one red is `nightly-status`, which grades main's scheduled slow run. The diff reaches nothing it reads, and the body answers it. `pr-contract` was green at 13:16:52Z, after the last other run concluded (Analyze (python), 13:15:58Z). The earlier head's red `pr-contract` (carry_audit UNROUTED) is answered in the body, so step 11 holds.
- Policy half: gate-scoping.md and its generated copies still owe tvofi's approving review. That is not mine to give.
- Minor, not blocking: `[ -n "${PREPR_RECORD_CLOSURES:-}" ]` means that `PREPR_RECORD_CLOSURES=0` opts in.

## Blocking

- **The arms pin the recorder's leader pid, not its process group, and the group is the load.** The watchdog's `kill -TERM -- -"$rpid"` and the `set -m` that gives the recorder its own group exist because `tests/derive_closures.sh` forks its recording lanes as `( ... ) &` (derive_closures.sh:235). Those lanes are the python recordings that fed the box's load. The self-test's sleeper has no child, and `reap_arm` checks only `$spid`. M7 changes one token, `kill -TERM -- -"$rpid"` to `kill -TERM "$rpid"`, and the self-test gives 323 passed, 0 failed (ev/mut-M7.txt).
  - I wrote my own probe (ev/lane-*.diff). It gives the sleeper one `( sleep 300 ) &` lane, as derive_closures.sh does, and adds the lane's state to `REAP`. A process counts as alive only when `ps -o stat=` shows something other than `Z`, because PID 1 in this container leaves zombies unreaped and `kill -0` counts them as alive. My first pass used `kill -0` and misread a zombie this way.
  - At the head, the probe passes all three reap arms with `gone:gone:lane-gone`. Under M7, all three fail with `gone:gone:lane-alive` (ev/lane-M7.txt). In both runs, the one other failure is my probe's own `| grep -qv`, caught by the pipefail lint.
  - So the head's code is right, but the test does not hold it. Its arms pass while the production orphan of the recorder's work comes back.
  - To unblock: make the sleeper fork a child, as the recorder does. Then require that child gone in every reap arm, and read it as gone by its state, not by `kill -0`. That last point is the zombie trap R10-UPDATE-PR-SIGNALS's brief records for this container. Carry: R10-PREPR-CAP (item 61eab2a5)
- **Step 6b's call site, the route this round changes, is not driven.** `drv.sh` evals prepr up to `rc=0` and then calls `closures_step` itself, so prepr.sh:2945 never runs under the arms. M9 puts that line back to the round-1 route, `CLOSURES_LINE=$(closures_line "$BASE")`, and the self-test still gives 323 passed, 0 failed (ev/mut-M9.txt).
  - That is the shape round 1 measured as deferring a TERM to the prepr until the recorder finishes. M4sub puts the same shape inside `closures_step`, and it fails the TERM-alone and group arms (321/2). So a one-line revert at the production site restores the round-1 defect with the suite green.
  - To unblock, either one fixes it: have the driver reach the recorder through step 6b's own statement, or add a static pin that 6b calls `closures_step` and runs no `$(closures_line`. M9 must then fail. Carry: R10-PREPR-CAP (item 3fc47a16)

- **The off-Linux default and the opt-in hold.** RESULT M1 gives 319/4, M2 gives 321/2 and M6 gives 322/1, each failing exactly the arms the body names. The minor finding from round 1 is fixed: `PREPR_RECORD_CLOSURES=0` no longer opts in, and M6 pins that. Carry: dismissed: confirmed as claimed (item 9c353878)
- **The roster's recommendation is dispositioned.** Round 1 noted it as undispositioned: force the opt-in on diffs touching `tests/closures.json` or `tests/closure.py`. The body now dispositions it: those diffs are case `full`, which 6b skips before the platform predicate is read. A `full`-case arm pins that skip. `cloud_relay.sh`'s handoff arm updated every open PR whose `handoff/<topic>` tip was ahead of its head, and nothing could exclude one. The roster PR's topic is `audit-r10-roster`. Every `roster_edit.py` push lands on that branch, forward-carries included, so freezing the roster PR meant stopping every roster push (K13a). This PR adds the hold that the study specifies:

- `<state>/cloud-handoff-hold` lists PR numbers, one per line. Blank lines and `#` lines are allowed. Only the orchestrator writes it. A last line with no trailing newline is read like any other.
- A listed PR whose handoff is ahead is not updated. The pass prints `cloud_relay: HELD #<pr> <handoff tip>` once. Removing the number resumes it.
- A missing or empty file holds nothing. The whole handoff arm is refused for that pass by any line that is not a plain PR number, or by a file that is not a readable regular file. The refusal is rc 2, `refused: malformed hold file`, and `OWED <utc> handoff-hold-malformed <file> -` in `<log>.level`. That line stays until a pass reads the file well-formed. A malformed file never holds all and never holds none.
- `cloud_relay.sh held <pr>` reads the same file through the same parser: rc 0 held, 1 not held, 2 malformed. R10-ORCH-MACHINERY's `handoff` job can therefore use it unchanged, with the same path, grammar and refusal.

Some design choices here could look like bugs to a later seat. Each is pinned by a check and a mutant:

- The hold is checked after the "handoff already contained in the PR head" test, so a held PR with nothing to apply prints nothing (`cloud_relay-9`).
- It is checked before the failed-update ledger, so a hold outranks a recorded failure (`cloud_relay-8`).
- A refusal stops only the handoff arm. The probe arm of `pass` still runs.
- The grammar is strict: no leading zeros and no trailing text. A lenient parse is how "hold nothing" happens silently.
- The malformed-file refusal is a level line, never an event-log line. `orchestrator_tick.py`'s `relay_owed` (#2547) skips any log `OWED` line that names no PR (`cloud_relay-10`). Every well-formed pass clears it (`cloud_relay-11`).

Mutant ids are per file, `cloud_relay-1` to `cloud_relay-11`, never new S numbers. This is the P6 convention in this group's brief.

Code-owned: no. `grep -n "cloud_relay\|tools/audit/seat\|r10_seat" .github/CODEOWNERS` prints nothing for `tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh`, `tools/audit/seat/INSTRUMENTS.md` and `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py`.

Group: R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE (registration pending: roster PR-B)

Spec: the pack group file `dev/programme/flow-study/roster/groups/R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE.json` at pin ff1beba2a24cab268cca5426cc390dbf21185cc0 (brief revision 7, (a) to (d) in one pull request: no fixer had started (a)), with STUDY.md K15 and its revision-7 table at the same pin.

The train's `--overlap` main gate (`Train.main_green`) counted every required context whose latest run had no green conclusion as red, so contexts still in flight were logged "is not green ... revert it first". Replayed on main e7c66485's live runs, the base logs exactly that line for three in-flight required contexts; this head logs "still running ... a wait, not red".

The fix gives `merge_train.py` one module-level state classifier, which the train, `merge_pr.sh` and the orchestrator tick all use (K15: "one owner"):

- (a) `latest_runs`, `run_state` and `classify(latest, required)` judge the latest run of each required context. A queued or in-progress run is `wait`, never red. A context with no run yet is `wait`. Red outranks wait. `NOT_GATING` (`record`, `record-autofix`, `nightly-status`, `delivery-status`) never counts, even if a ruleset lists it. `required` None raises: an unreadable ruleset is a refusal, never green. The `--overlap` gate logs RED (with the revert text) only on red, a wait otherwise, and "check runs unreadable" when the read failed. `wait_ci(only=...)` judges through the same `classify`.
- (b) `stale(cr, run_status)`: a check-run that is queued or in progress while its workflow run (from `details_url`) has completed is stale. `Train.unstale(h)` runs in `land()` before the first merge attempt. It re-runs each stale workflow run once (two stale check-runs of one run re-run it once), logs `STALE <context> at <h> ... run <id>`, and re-reads until the context concludes. If the context is still red or unconcluded, the train stops. `merge_train.py unstale <sha>` is the same step, and `merge_pr.sh` calls it (`unstale_head`) before its CI wait.
- (c) `conflicts(run, base, head)` reads the conflicted paths from `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only --no-messages` under GitHub's merge: `text_merge(run)` puts git's own text merge in place of every merge driver the clone's config defines (`git config --get-regexp '^merge\..+\.driver$'`), because GitHub runs none. So a claim file the local claimnotes driver would resolve is still listed: GitHub reports that head DIRTY, and the driver is its repair. An unreadable config is no answer (None). `build()` uses the same `text_merge`. `dirty_repair(files, claim_files)` offers the claimnotes repair only when every conflicted file is a claim file. Anything else is a content conflict: it goes back to the owning fixer, and its verdict does not carry. The tick's DIRTY line names those files first (#2569's shape: `roster_edit.py`).
- (d) A head is reviewable exactly when `classify(...)[2]` is empty. The claimnotes driver every clone installs (`claim-files.md`) ran inside `git merge-tree`, resolved a notes-only claim conflict and printed `MERGE-CLAIM: resolved <path>` to stderr, and `Tick.git` returns stdout plus stderr. A claim-only DIRTY read "could not answer", and a content-plus-claim conflict listed the MERGE-CLAIM line as a file. Now no driver runs, which is what GitHub does.

Alternatives considered and rejected:
- A new `ci_state.py` module would mean a second import path for `queue_pre_flight.py`, which already imports the train for its words, and a new self-testing file to wire.
- Keeping `Tick.judge` and adding a train-side copy would be the second rule the brief forbids.
- Re-running every non-completed check before a merge would be a guess where the workflow run's own status is the fact.
- In (c), parsing GitHub's `mergeStateStatus` alone cannot name the files.
- In (c), reading stdout alone in the tick: it removes the symptom and leaves the driver running, so a claim-only conflict would still read clean locally (`[]`, "re-read GitHub's state") while GitHub reports it DIRTY. With no driver run, the driver's stderr has no producer. The strict parse stays as the backstop: a clean exit with a second line, or a conflict exit with none, is None. A stdout-only runner would also be a site no arm can kill, because a neutralized merge-tree writes nothing to stderr.
- In (c), neutralizing only the drivers base's `.gitattributes` names, as `build()` did: a driver named only in the head's attributes, or set in `.git/info/attributes`, would still run. Only a configured driver can run (an attribute naming none falls back to the text merge), so the config is the complete set. `build()` and `conflicts()` share that one rule.

2589.body:
R10-FLY-GH-READ-RETRY, PR 1 of 2: `tools/pr/app_approve.sh`'s GitHub reads retry with a bounded backoff, and only on failures that a later read can ride out.

Train 8 stopped on `app_approve: REFUSE: could not read pull request #2547` after a long CI wait: one `gh api` call with no retry, stderr not kept. The roster brief counts it as the third instance of "one unretried GitHub read kills an instrument".

What changes, in `tools/pr/app_approve.sh`:

- **`gh_read <var> <gh api args...>`** is the one entry for the four reads (the pull request, read twice by `check_pr`; the comments, `--paginate`; `.github/CODEOWNERS` at `ref=main`; the changed files, `--paginate`). On a refusal it returns 1 with gh's stderr in `GH_ERR`, and every `die` at those sites names it.
- **`gh_transient <stderr>`** classifies a failure from gh's stderr. The deciding line is the last whole status line, `gh: <message> (HTTP NNN)` or `gh: HTTP NNN`, kept whole as `<code> <line>` by one sed (`s/^gh: (.*\()?HTTP ([0-9]{3})\)?$/\2 &/p | tail -1`). Retried:
  - a 5xx or 429 status;
  - a 403 whose own status line holds `secondary rate limit`, in any case (`9b9770b34`: the phrase is read on that line alone, `printf '%s\n' "$status" | grep -qi`);
  - with no status line, a transport line anywhere in stderr starting `Get "http(s)://...": ` or `error connecting to `.

  Everything else refuses after its one call.
- **Budget is `app_push.sh`'s read-back rule**: 4 reads, settling `READ_SLEEP * 3^(n-1)` = 5/15/45 s, each printed; a spent budget refuses with the last error and `(after 4 attempts)`. A wrong answer is never retried (callers judge a completed read). Writes are never retried: the mint, the review POST and the revoke stay single `curl` calls.

2605.body:
Builds countermeasure A of `dev/audit/rca/nightly-ha-pyspy-timeout.md` (#2479) in `tests/nightly_ha.py`. **It does not remove the `stable` red, and the real-HA measurement says why: the hang is per process, not per sample.** It lands what is sound: a cheaper red and a bounded retry, each pinned. The per-process residual goes to R10-NIGHTLY-HB-RESPAWN (decision O-4).

Delivery-status: group R10-NIGHTLY-PYSPY-RETRY.

Round 2 repairs round 1's `blocked mutation-vacuous` verdict (`review/2605`, `VERDICT.md`, reviewed head `7651b942…`):

- The real lane's cut is now pinned. The real boot passes no `spy_timeout`, so the cut is `LoopHeartbeat`'s constructor default. `tests/entities.py` now checks that this default `is PY_SPY_TIMEOUT_S`. It also checks that `_async_hb_measure` injects no `spy_timeout` of its own. X5 (default `30.0`) and X2 (`PY_SPY_TIMEOUT_S = 25.0`) are now killed.
- The whole-control bound is pinned. `HB_CONTROL_TRIES * (HB_CONTROL_HOLD_S + HB_CONTROL_REST_S)` must be `< 22.0` s. At this head it is 21.75 s.
- Two behaviour pins are added:
  - The control rests between tries. Two tries with a 1 s rest must take at least the rest plus both spins. This kills X1.
  - The control survives two hung samples and answers on try 3. This kills X3 (`HB_CONTROL_TRIES = 2`).
- The constants' comment at `PY_SPY_TIMEOUT_S` / `HB_CONTROL_TRIES` was corrected. It now says the fresh-spin retry was measured **not** to rescue a real-HA hang (F6, F7). It also says what the retry is kept for: a bounded cost per red, and a retry rather than a fail when a try's sample came back late, missed the spin or answered rc≠0.

What the PR changes, from the base:

- `py-spy dump --nonblocking` is cut at `PY_SPY_TIMEOUT_S` = 5 s instead of 30 s. The RCA measured a healthy sample at ≤ 0.15 s on 710 of 710 in-image samples. That is a small synthetic process, not real HA.
- `hb:positive_control` now runs `_async_hb_control`:
  - It makes up to `HB_CONTROL_TRIES` = 3 fresh spins, with `HB_CONTROL_REST_S` = 1 s of loop time between them.
  - Each spin is sampled once and held until that sample returns, bounded by `HB_CONTROL_HOLD_S` = 6.25 s.
  - It stops at the first try in which the gap, the in-process stack and py-spy's rc=0 section all name `_hb_spin`.
  - `check_hb_positive_control` takes the list of tries and passes only when a single try reads all three.

What is pinned, and what is not:

- Pinned in `tests/entities.py`:
  - Per spin: `HB_DUMP_S + PY_SPY_TIMEOUT_S <= HB_CONTROL_HOLD_S < HB_HANG_S` (60 s).
  - Whole control, every try hung: `HB_CONTROL_TRIES * (HB_CONTROL_HOLD_S + HB_CONTROL_REST_S) < 22` s, against the base's 30 s for one sample. The control rests only between tries, so the tighter figure is 3 × 6.25 + 2 × 1 = 20.75 s.
  - Tries: at least 3, by the two-hang pin.
- Not pinned as a figure: any other stall's dump, which costs at most `HB_MAX_DUMPS` × `PY_SPY_TIMEOUT_S` = 3 × 5 s. That is derived, not measured. Its two factors are bounded by pins: the default cut is the constant, and the whole-control pin forces `PY_SPY_TIMEOUT_S` ≤ 5.08 s at 3 tries.
- Values left free, and why:
  - `PY_SPY_TIMEOUT_S` below 5 s: a cut shorter than a healthy sample times out every try and fails the control loudly, never silently.
  - `HB_CONTROL_REST_S` within the bound: only that a rest happens is pinned, because F7 measured that no rest length rescues a hang.
  - `HB_CONTROL_TRIES` above 3: refused by the 22 s pin, since 4 tries give 29 s.

The first design, measured and replaced: hold one spin and retry py-spy up to 3 times inside it. A real-HA run hung on 3 of 3 attempts inside one held spin (F6), so I replaced it with the try-level retry. Alternatives considered:

- A retry without the hold: the retried sample would read the idle loop and could never name the spin.
- A blocking-mode fallback and a raised timeout: priced under the residual below.

## Disclosed: what this cannot fix

- In 140 real-py-spy heartbeat runs at the two retrying designs (F6 + F7 + F9), 3 hang episodes occurred. Under the two non-blocking designs, every retry the code made hung:
  - in-spin retries: 3 of 3 hung (F6);
  - fresh-spin retries 1 s apart: 3 of 3 hung (F7);
  - the experimental blocking fallback (F9) answered, but only after the process was stopped for 38.5 s.
- If samples hung independently at the RCA's ≈ 7 %, two further hangs in one episode would have P ≈ 0.07² ≈ 0.005. Two episodes, each with both further samples hung, would have P ≈ 2.4e-5 (F10). The hang therefore holds for the life of the HA process. **This PR does not lower the ≈ 7 % false-red rate on `stable`**; it lowers what each red costs.
- The countermeasure that addresses a per-process hang is a container respawn on an all-tries py-spy timeout. Under decision O-4 it is group R10-NIGHTLY-HB-RESPAWN, which runs after this group, and it is not built here (Forward-carry).

## Root cause

`dev/audit/rca/nightly-ha-pyspy-timeout.md`, #2479. This PR builds that RCA's countermeasure A, and it falsifies one of A's premises. The RCA expected "a first attempt that times out, followed by a second rc=0 naming the spin". That is the behaviour of the stub. On real HA the further attempts hung too (F6, F7).

2606.body:
Root-cause record for the recurring "API rate limit exceeded for installation" reds on required checks (arch-score, pr-contract, env-matrix, validate-hacs; 2026-10-22 about 06:27Z, 08:40Z, 09:44:27Z). It records only; no workflow is changed. The analysis is `dev/audit/rca/install-ratelimit.md`, with an offline harness, `dev/audit/harnesses/record_api_calls.sh`, that counts the REST calls Governance's `record` job makes per push to main. Round 2: rewritten after the fix review's claim-refuted block.

- **Cause.** Every job that went red reads with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, one installation bucket shared by every workflow in the repository; HANDOVER item 44's "App quota" is another bucket. **The bucket's size is unmeasured.** GitHub documents 1,000 an hour, and round 1 took that as the limit, but Governance run `39745228063`'s record job (job `119711895503`) completed full walks (84 PRs, `RECORD_ENUM: api`, no 403) after two earlier push runs in the same minutes. The four push runs from 08:03:46Z to 08:07:08Z all succeeded and demanded 3,030 calls by the formula below, so at least about 3,030 calls were served from 08:03:46Z. That is a lower bound, not the limit. The 83 % and the 3.2 to 4.6 times the bucket are withdrawn.
- **The heaviest consumer is `governance.yml` `record`.** It runs on every push to main and walks `<last tag>..origin/main` three times (`--record`, `--stats`, `--sunset`), costing `3W + 6P` calls: 834 at `04c1dd779` by the harness, 825 by the live job at `c409c9b18` (91 PRs over 93 commits). That is hundreds of calls per push to main, against tens per PR head for the follower, pr-contract, arch-score and validate-hacs. The 08:38 record job (run `39749268769`) degraded after the 08Z burst: histograms step 15 s instead of about 112 s, friction filer failed after 0 s.
- **Bursts.** Each red fell in an hour of five or more pushes to main: 06Z, 6 pushes including the direct push `b787c7d45` (06:35Z), demand 4,305; 08Z, 6 pushes, 4,599; 09Z, 5 pushes including `04c1dd779` (#2604, 09:42Z, about 90 s before the 09:44:27Z red), 4,080.

comments.body:
Fix review: blocked 83d21ff832455462268f1d9ce9d75c17a1209d07 claim-refuted: the 1,000/hr bucket, the 83 % and the 3.2-4.6x are contradicted by Governance run 39745228063, where the record job read its whole window cleanly after two earlier pushes in the same minutes

bus-nonce: 85617c2d23cec9918f429629cd2c2d8f

Round 1 of the fix review for #2606 (root-cause record, R10-RCA-INSTALL-RATELIMIT). Reviewed head 83d21ff832455462268f1d9ce9d75c17a1209d07 (authored code head 0a8c4523a76a1154bb634ce24c9dc110f1b170a8 plus the delivery-row commit), base 04c1dd77990b97ae144e48cd29655853783532f2. Every figure below was taken at that base, in a private clone with refs/remotes/origin/main pointed at it. The roles/ directory is unchanged between the merge base and origin/main.

## Block

The call counts are real. The denominator they are divided by is not established, and the log of a run the record itself cites refutes it.

What the PR states as fact: "One push to main uses 83 % of the repository's hourly GITHUB_TOKEN bucket", "each burst asked 3.2 to 4.6 times the bucket", and `install-ratelimit.md` 1.1 "its limit is 1,000 requests per hour per repository". Section 1.1 itself says the `x-ratelimit-limit` header was not measured; the body drops that hedge.

What the logs show (ev/record_job_runs_0803_0912.txt, ev/record_job_08z_extract.txt):

- Governance push runs 39744954535, 39745082624, 39745228063 and 39745375894 (merges b980e2fa0, 1787ffd08, fae523a14, c61659318 at 08:03:46Z, 08:04:49Z, 08:05:57Z, 08:07:08Z) all concluded success. By the record's own formula they demand 744 + 753 + 762 + 771 = 3,030 calls inside about four minutes, all on `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- The third of them, record job 119711895503 (08:06:01 to 08:10:42), has `RECORD_ENUM: api`, `RECORD: 84 merged pull request(s)`, a `--stats` pass that parsed 84 PRs, and a `--sunset` pass, with step times 35 s / 112 s / 110 s: full walks, no `403`, no `rate limit` text, no `merge-enumeration` skip. Under a shared 1,000/hr bucket, that job could not have completed its own 762 calls after runs 1 and 2 (1,497 between them) had been served in the same hour. The two earlier runs concluded success, and the failing job at 08:38 (below) shows what a dry bucket does to this job, so they did not run degraded.
- The record job at 08:38 (run 39749268769, job 119725423893) did degrade: refusal step 41 s (full), histograms step 15 s instead of about 112 s, friction-filer step failed after 0 s. So the bucket was dry by 08:39 and the record job is a heavy consumer, but the size at which it ran dry is not 1,000. By the record's own demand figures, at least 3,030 calls were served from 08:03:46 and the next job to starve was the 08:38 one, after about 3,900 (744+753+762+771+780+89); other consumers add to that. The data fit a limit in the thousands, not 1,000, and do not say which.

Consequences that need rewriting, not only re-wording:

1. Section 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3, the body's Cause bullet and its Figures list state 83 %, 3.2-4.6x and "1,000 requests an hour" as findings. They are a model on an assumed limit, which one cited log contradicts. The calls per push (834, 1,065, 0) stay as they are.
2. Section 4's sufficiency argument ("M1 + M2 = 3 x 370 = 1,110, still over 1,000, so M3") rests on the same number. Until M0 prints the real limit, whether M1 + M2 suffice is open, and the owner decision O-1 / M3 in the roster brief for R10-RECORD-API-BUDGET is decided on a premise the log refutes. The record should say M0 comes first and the M3 call waits for its number.
3. The reason section 1 gives for ranking the record job first (hundreds of calls per main push against tens per head) survives, and the 08:38 degradation supports it. State it as that, with the limit unknown.
4. The burst table in 1.3 omits the push of 04c1dd779 (#2604, 09:42Z), which is the push 90 s before the 09:44:27Z arch-score red, and the direct push b787c7d45 at 06:35Z. The "4 pushes, 09:03-09:26" row is five pushes in the 09Z hour.

To lift the block: restate the bucket size as unmeasured and cite run 39745228063 against 1,000; recompute or withdraw 83 % and 3.2-4.6x; make M3 conditional on M0's measured limit; correct the burst table. Nothing else in the PR needs to move.

## Findings

- The harness reads 0 silently when it has no data. In a checkout whose origin is not a github remote, `policy_lint.mjs` falls back to the `subject` enumerator with `RECORD_ENUM: subject (no github remote on origin)`, nothing calls `curl`, and `record_api_calls.sh` prints `TOTAL 0` and exits 0 (ev/harness_no_github_remote.txt). The fixer's proof for the countermeasure is "reads 834, must read 370 or less", and a 0 meets that, and the null control reads 0 for a different reason. The harness should refuse a zero on a non-empty window. Carry: R10-RECORD-API-BUDGET
- The harness counts a partial abort as a count. It exits only when the output contains `curl failed`; any other `fetchError` (`HTTP 403 from ...`, `unparseable JSON ...`) ends a mode early and the early count is printed as the mode's total. Mutant: replace the reviews read at policy_lint.mjs:3316 with a bare array, which the caller reads as a failed fetch, and `--stats` and `--sunset` read 96 each instead of 278 (ev/mutant_drop_reviews.txt), with exit 0. Exactly the shape a real 403 produces. Carry: R10-RECORD-API-BUDGET
- Section 4's M1 + M2 estimate understates the runs. "Burst of 5 runs it twice" and "3 x 370" assume the job still lasts about 6 minutes. M1 cuts it to about 155 s (370 calls at 0.42 s), and the pending slot then drains faster: replaying the 08Z pushes (08:03:46, 08:04:49, 08:05:57, 08:07:08, 08:09:21, 08:38:37) with a 155 s job and one running plus one pending gives 5 runs, about 1,850 calls, not 3. M2 and M1 pull against each other, so the count after both has to be measured by the fixer, not carried from this record. Carry: R10-RECORD-API-BUDGET
- The roster brief for R10-RECORD-API-BUDGET (2a64d2b5e) records M3 as decision O-1 taken "under the mandate". Given the block above, O-1 must be taken after M0's measured limit, and the brief should say so as a precondition of the fixer's design. Carry: R10-RECORD-API-BUDGET
- 834 is the policy_lint reads only. The record job also runs the friction filer and sweep through `gh` with the same token (about 17 calls in the 09:30 log, 6 + 11 listing and view reads); the harness comment says "before policy-docs, env-matrix and the other jobs" but the filer sits inside the same job. Carry: dismissed: about 20 calls against 834, already disclosed in the harness header, moves no conclusion

## Evidence

- RESULT harness, base 04c1dd779, default window v7.0.2..origin/main: `--record 94`, `--stats 370`, `--sunset 370`, `TOTAL 834`. v7.0.1 window: 121 / 472 / 472, `TOTAL 1065`. Empty window (origin/main): `TOTAL 0`. All three match the body (ev/harness_base.txt). The formula holds: W = 94, P = 92, 3W + 6P = 834.
- RESULT counts: `git rev-list --first-parent --count v7.0.2..origin/main` = 94; merges = 92, at 04c1dd779. Matches.
- RESULT mutation of the harness's subject. Dropping the reviews read in policy_lint.mjs cleanly (a well-formed empty result): TOTAL 650 (94 / 278 / 278). Dropping the `sunset` mode from the loop: TOTAL 464. Both move the figure from 834 and both restored cleanly (ev/mutant_drop_reviews2.txt, ev/mutant_drop_mode.txt). The null control reads 0 for an empty window with a github remote set.
- RESULT bursts, from `git log --first-parent` committer times converted to UTC: 06:07, 06:08, 06:09, 06:10, 06:11Z (5 pushes, 3W+6P = 696 to 732, sum 3,570); 08:03, 08:04, 08:05, 08:07, 08:09Z plus 08:38Z (6 pushes, 744 to 789, sum 4,599); 09:03, 09:17, 09:24, 09:26Z (4 pushes, 798 to 825, sum 3,246), then 09:42Z (834). The three sums reproduce 3,570, about 4,600 and about 3,250, and the ratios 3.2 to 4.6 follow arithmetically from them against 1,000; the 1,000 is the unsupported part (see Block). The pushes per UTC hour on 2026-10-22: 00Z 1, 01Z 3, 02Z 3, 04Z 2, 06Z 6, 08Z 6, 09Z 5; the "two or more pushes in 6 of the 10 hours from 00Z to 10Z (01, 02, 04, 06, 08, 09)" count reproduces (ev/pushes_per_hour_utc.txt).
- RESULT live job at c409c9b18 (run 39755501453, job 119746351603): `RECORD_ENUM: api`, `RECORD: 91 merged pull request(s)`, W = 93 by `git rev-list`, step times 09:27:59 to 09:28:42 (GAP/record), 09:28:42 to 09:30:32 (stats), 09:30:40 to 09:33:15 (sunset). Matches 91 PRs over 93 commits and the 44 / 153 / 155 s figures. 3W + 6P = 825.
- RESULT workflow files at 04c1dd779: arch-score.yml:56, pr-contract.yml:133/178/243/272 and governance.yml (env-matrix at 926, policy-docs at 183/223, record at 1147/1167/1210/1217) map `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`; pr-contract-rerun.yml:70/123 use `github.token`. validate.yml maps no token itself (hacs/action's default); I could not confirm from the tree that it uses `github.token`, so that row is not re-derived. `record` has `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.event_name != 'merge_group'`, and the workflow's concurrency group for non-pull_request events is the run id, so no run is ever coalesced. 1,000/hr is GitHub's documented figure for the default token, but that is not measured in this repository and one cited log contradicts it (Block).
- RESULT job 119753501292 (arch-score on #2580, 09:44:27Z) log: `gh: API rate limit exceeded for installation ... (HTTP 403)` at the first `gh api repos/.../pulls/2580` read, with `GH_TOKEN` from `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`. The red is external to this PR.
- RESULT governance push runs failing on 2026-10-22: 01cf1398a, 8a4c438e7, 04c1dd779 (the record names these three), and also 07fcbee2e and 6077bf70e at 02:5xZ and b787c7d45 (06:35Z). I read only the 8a4c438e7 job: the failure is the friction-filer step after a 15 s histograms step, the shape of a failed fetch. The record's "their failing step was not read here" stands for the other two.
- RESULT process state (c) and cost test, judged as written. State (c) is accepted: HANDOVER 44 and R10-FOLLOWER-DEBOUNCE diagnosed this class and were followed, and the unit was runs not calls; the countermeasure (M0) changes the unit. The cost test's arithmetic is sound (3 instances a day, at least 1 h of train each, standing cost zero to 2 s) and does not depend on the bucket size; it passes. What the block touches is the sufficiency argument, not the verdict that a countermeasure is worth building.
- RESULT cause ranking: the record job is not shown to be the only consumer, but it is the one whose per-event cost scales with the window, no other reader found in section 3 does, and the 08:38 degraded run follows 3,000 demanded calls in the 08Z hour. That much stands.
- RESULT forward carries on handoff/audit-r10-roster (2a64d2b5e): R10-FLY-GH-READ-RETRY 9326f8a4e and R10-CI-LAYOUT-P2 d9f33a0f2 are ancestors, the group R10-RECORD-API-BUDGET is appended with after R10-RCA-INSTALL-RATELIMIT, M0 to M2 and decision O-1. `carry_audit.py check` over the body: `2 finding item(s): 2 routed, 0 unrouted, 0 bad destination(s)` (ev/carry_audit_body.txt). The FLY carry states its requirement (wait for the reset the 403 names, never loop) but no control; it is a one-line requirement for a fixer who has the PR 1 proof in the same brief, so I did not block on it.
- RESULT merge: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 83d21ff83...` exits clean, tree c399060df503e22e5def4808760e72c742dfe43a, no MERGE-CLAIM line (ev/merge_tree.txt). origin/main at review time cd4aaed44 (v7.0.3 stamp).
- RESULT versions and claims: the diff is four files (the record, the harness, tests/closures.json INERT entry for the harness, the delivery row); VERSION, the manifest version and the notes heading are untouched; no claim file moved. No workflow changed.
- RESULT check-runs at the head, read at 10:27Z and again at 10:33Z: success for pr-contract, arch-score (both), validate-hacs, env-matrix, policy-docs, wave-script, instrument-self-tests, delivery-status, budget-raise-gate, hassfest, mutation, briefs, closure-scope, scope, typing, browser, Analyze (javascript-typescript), Analyze (actions); skipped record, delivery-status-publish, kernel-points, nightly-ha, mutation-pins, mutation-autofix; CodeQL neutral; still in progress at 10:33Z: closures, coverage, fast (3.14), Analyze (python). I did not re-run any heavy lane. No run is red with "API rate limit exceeded".
- RESULT nightly-status is red at this head. It is not a required check and does not block, and this diff does not reach what it reads (defect-root-cause.md). The body's "Red checks: none" was accepted by pr-contract (success).
- RESULT the mutation lane is green because the diff writes no production code line; no mutant was drawn (fix-review.md 11). Step 1 of the role is n/a for a record, and the harness mutants above are the instrument check.

2612.body:
R10-SOLVER, wave 17, round 2. One value-neutral performance fix (D9-s1-01) and a recorded disposition for the P4 class issue (D0-s1-01, D0-s2-01). This PR measures P4 and does not change it in production.

Closes #2240.
Part of #2250.

**1. N-solve-recompute (#2250, D9-s1-01).** L-BFGS-B asks for the value and the gradient at every point it visits. The multi-start's own runs already took both from one batch (R9 D9-s1-02). The two runs that move a start did not. These are the two-zone half-price continuation (`_optimize_space_only.move_starts`) and the relaxed duty-cycle candidate (`_relaxed_starts`). Each passed the scalar `objective` as `fun`, plus a jac that called it again as the difference's base, so every gradient cost two scalar horizons on top of the batch. All four run sites now go through one driver helper, `_lbfgsb_run(objective, batch_objective, x0, bounds, args, maxiter, memo=None)`: the multi-start start, its polish in `_lbfgsb_restart`, the continuation and the relaxed candidate. Wherever `_bounds_supported_by_batch` serves the bounds, the helper builds the fused, memoized `fun` itself and passes `jac=True`. Otherwise it leaves the estimate to scipy, as before. The stop (`ftol 1e-6`) and the finite-difference step (`_LBFGSB_FD_EPS = 1e-4`) are each spelled once. `_lbfgsb_run` reads the step both for the fused batch gradient and for the `eps` option, so the two cannot disagree (review O2). `_multi_start_minimize` loses its `fd_eps` keyword, and its shared evaluation memo is passed as `memo`. A batched row is bitwise the scalar objective (#97), so no iterate moves. The plan is bit-identical, and no golden or stress scenario moves (Figures).

This is the architect note's shape: "one fused objective call" in the driver, touching only the minimiser driver and the objective-evaluation seam. Alternatives considered:
- Fuse only the two start-moving sites with a second helper. Rejected because it added a fourth spelling of the same run shape: `tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff` read `duplication_copies 40 -> 41`, which is inadmissible. One helper for all four reads `dS +0.0000 NULL`.
- Use the finder's own rewrite, `cont_fuse.py`'s fused arm, which wraps only the continuation. Rejected for the same reason, and it leaves the relaxed candidate unfused.
- Keep round 1's shape, where the callers build the fused callable and pass it in. Rejected on review O2: the step was spelled at each start-moving call site, in `_multi_start_minimize`'s `fd_eps` and in the options, and mutant J (a call-site step 1e-4 -> 1e-3) survived every check.

**2. P4 (#2240): seeds and stop tolerance. Disposition: duplicate of the owner's refusals #1293 (stop) and #1294 (seeds), re-measured at merge base `738d950aa` in round 1. No production change.** The owner refuted tightening the L-BFGS-B stop on #1293 (2026-09-22): "improves the objective (-0.332%) but loses +6.4% money on the backtest shoulder cell ... no intermediate ftol (3e-7..1e-9) captures the win without the loss, and the tighter rule costs 2.4x thread CPU". #1294 refused the production anchor ladder on cost. RCA-BULK-1 section 4 records both refusals as the class disposition: "A gap closable only by a refused knob is a duplicate of that refusal."
- **D0-s2-01 is the stop.** The finder's `ftol_race.py` read `polish_gap_winter_mean=0.0343 pct` (max 0.2281, drop-max mean 0.0066), down from 0.2025 % at the finding's baseline. Closing it means a tighter stop, which is #1293. The round's own closed loop at ftol 1e-10 (`dev/audit/rounds/round10/D0/s2/mpc_mask_ftol.out`) realises worse money in 3 of 4 cells (-0.80 %, -1.50 %, flat -0.65 %).
- **D0-s1-01 is the seeds.** `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_solver_seed_or_stop.py` splits `race.py`'s c1 into a seeds-only arm and a restart-only arm (a fresh run from the shipped x). Over the 23 cells `race.py` reports above 1e-3, restart-only recovers at most 1.008e-4 in 22, so the stop is not their cause. The 23rd, tz0 summer_typical/summer_cool, is a stop cell: restart-only recovers its whole 1.829e-3 (a 0.43 SEK bill, dSEK 0.005, under the D0 brief's money bar). Seeds-only recovers more than 9e-4 in 22 of 23 cells and is 5.976e-3 worse than production in the remaining one. That is the seed ladder #1294 refused.
- **The narrower stop change #1293 did not measure was priced and lost.** This is a single extra `_lbfgsb_restart` of the multi-start's winner at ftol 1e-9, adopted only past `_LBFGSB_RESTART_KEEP_REL`. `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_solver_winner_polish.py` measured its realised one-day closed-loop money:
  - non-flat mean +0.1462 % cheaper, but 1 of 6 non-flat cells worse (winter_typical/winter_mild -0.99 %, bought with comfort);
  - flat-price null -0.7893 %.

  A stop change that loses money on a flat price is #1293's mechanism, so it is not shipped.

The finder harnesses therefore read identical at both ends (Figures). This PR leaves the measured quantity alone on purpose.

## Mutation proof

The block run is `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/seat/features_block.py "# -- R10-SOLVER: N-solve-recompute" "# -- R9 N-fit-integrator (#1672)"`. At head it prints `ALL 5 FEATURES BLOCK PASSED`. Each mutant was written to `optimizer.py` by a scratch runner and restored after its run; `filecmp` against the saved copy read `restored True`.
- A, `_lbfgsb_run`'s guard without `_bounds_supported_by_batch` (review O1): rc=1. FAIL `R10-SOLVER (O1): bounds _bounds_supported_by_batch refuses run on scipy's own estimate -- no batch call, the plain scalar run's point` [batch calls refused=3 served=4].
- J1, `_LBFGSB_FD_EPS = 1e-3`: rc=1. FAIL `(null, exact)` [max |dP| 2.146e+00 kW] and FAIL `(O1)`.
- J2, the fused gradient's step only -> 1e-3 (the review's mutant J, now at its one site): rc=1. FAIL `(null, exact)` [max |dP| 2.146e+00 kW].
- J3, the `eps` option only -> 1e-3: rc=1. FAIL `(O1)` [x 0.6995 vs plain 0.69995]. A fused run never reads that option, so only the scalar arm sees it.
- Review J as written (a start-site step) has no site left: `git grep -n "1e-4" -- custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py` names one step literal, the `_LBFGSB_FD_EPS` assignment.
- GUARD_OFF (`if False:`): rc=1. FAIL census precondition [{}] and FAIL `(O1)`.
- BOOLOP (`and` -> `or`): rc=1. FAIL `(O1)` [batch calls refused=3 served=4].
- The continuation passes `None` for the batch: rc=1. FAIL census precondition and FAIL `(positive control)`.
- The relaxed candidate passes `None` for the batch: rc=1. FAIL census precondition and FAIL `(positive control)`.
- Review G (`_lbfgsb_restart` passes `None` for the batch) passes the block: rc=0, `ALL 5 FEATURES BLOCK PASSED`, multi-start (6, 0). It is killed in the whole of `tests/features.py`: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` rc=1, `1 of 4306 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`: FAIL `R9-F2.2 D9-s1-02: a batched solve never evaluates the scalar objective inside L-BFGS-B` [scalar calls inside minimize: batched 78, unbatched (null arm) 299].
- `_memoized_value_and_gradient`'s `if memo is None:` -> `if False:` (the site the deleted triage called equivalent): rc=1. FAIL census precondition [{'relaxed': (1, 0)}], FAIL `(null, exact)` [max |dP| 3.656e+00 kW], `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'`.

The round-1 block on `738d950aa`'s `optimizer.py` read `{'relaxed': (1, 134), 'continuation': (1, 234), 'multi-start': (12, 0)}` and FAILed `... no L-BFGS-B run with a supplied jac simulates the scalar trajectory` (round 1's figure, reproduced by the reviewer's `ev/testfirst_revert.out`).

## Unpinned sites

`PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py --base origin/main` names three added sites:

## Null control

- Flat-price null, both arms, re-run in the reviewer's shape: `probe/rev-2612-b73e3ccc:ev/flat_null.py` (sha1 be8f89b66fd9ac33845bd19cbe9bacc4236a8eb4; the head adaptation, sha1 4c3c86476bfef42d2955db16f13d8e3d4db0476a, is a scratch probe). At the head, its `scalar_valued` arm takes the head's `_lbfgsb_run` signature and builds the gradient with `_fused_value_and_gradient(batch_objective, bounds, 1e-4)`. Its other three lines are unchanged. Run as `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 flat_null.py` at `a6e53320b` (the reviewer's file) and at `ec321cb76` and `7527c746d` (the adapted file), in this seat:
  - `prices=flat weather=winter_cold two_zone=True`: `identical=True max_dP=0.000e+00`, sha `282f8b7c5a56` in both arms at both heads.
  - `prices=flat weather=winter_mild two_zone=True`: `identical=True`, `f81494aeb061` in both arms at both heads.
  - `prices=flat weather=winter_cold two_zone=False`: `identical=True`, `e47e0996094f` in both arms at both heads.
  - Non-flat companion `winter_typical`: `identical=True`, `9b27e4b3a20d` in both arms at both heads.
  - The plan is byte-identical across O2 and between the arms. The hashes differ from the reviewer's (`f09d318e5598`, ...) because they were taken in another environment. Both ends here ran in this one: `/opt/hpo/venv-ci`, `OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Haswell`.

Positive control of the meter: the scalar-valued arm reads `{'relaxed': (1, 67), 'continuation': (1, 117), 'multi-start': (12, 491)}`.

The winner-polish arm's flat cells read -0.7893 % money.

## Figures

Seat venv `/opt/hpo/venv-ci` (python 3.14.7, numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1), linux x86_64, `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub`. Base is the merge base `58730d09f` in its own worktree. Counts and objectives are deterministic. CPU was not re-taken quiet (load1 3.25 and 3.44), so this body states no CPU figure.

2620.body:
The plan narrative now prices money in the price feed's currency (`coordinator.currency`), like every other money surface. Before this change, `_narrative_view` resolved the currency itself with `resolve_currency(hass)`, which returns the instance's label currency. A EUR feed on a SEK instance therefore published EUR sensors next to a narrative written in SEK. The local precedence is deleted, and the view reads the one value that `currency.py`'s `declared_currency` decides and the coordinator adopts on each cycle. The `narrative.render` docstring justified that local precedence ("A narrative line is recorded nowhere, so it can simply follow the instance"), and it is rewritten to state the new contract (fixer.md step 9).

The price-units comment in `_audit_price_units` named a nonexistent ``money_currency``. It now names what the sensors actually carry: `unit_of_measurement` and the `currency` attribute. The comment in `_raise_cop_issue` said the notice is priced "in the instance currency"; it is priced in the feed's, and the comment now says so.

Fixes #2243
Fixes #2222

#2243 is D14-s3-01, with D14-s2-01 merged into it. #2222 is D5-s3-01.

### Round 3: the seam cut is paid by a real move (orchestrator decision, mandate 6329234399, session s4)

The narrative's read of `self.currency` from the `views` seam costs `seam_cut_total` +1, because `currency` is stored only by `core` units. Round 2 paid it with a local alias in `_raise_cop_issue`, and review blocked that as metric-gamed: an alias cuts an occurrence count and no coupling. The orchestrator withdrew that route. This round:

- **The alias is gone.** `_raise_cop_issue` reads `self.currency` twice, as at the base. The corrected comment and the narrative fix stay.
- **The payment is a move.** `_scores_view` (`views`) reached into two private attributes of the `learning` seam, `_cop_baseline` and `_cop_health_cusum`, to recompute a watched-bucket count that `_learning_view` (`learning`) also computes, with a different guard (`_learning_view` checks `np.isfinite`, `_scores_view` did not). A new `learning` method, `_cop_watch()`, returns both the watched-bucket count and the Cusum's share of the alarm. `_learning_view` and `_scores_view` both call it, and `tests/seam_map.json` places it in `learning` (fixer.md step 12). The views seam now asks the COP watch for its grade through one call instead of reading the watch's state. The count has one definition, and the coordinator class is 10 lines shorter.
- **No budget is raised.** Step (3) of the brief, the conditional `seam_cut_total` raise, does not apply. `seam_cut_total` measures 707 against a budget of 708, and `class_excess_loc` and `max_class_loc` drop 11 each. `tests/structure.py` exits 2 on an unrecorded gain, so the three gains are recorded downward with `tests/structure.py --record`, in their own commit with the reason in its message. No row moves up.
- **Against #2647.** At origin/main `a7cf60cfd`, #2647 (R10-SCORES, which raises `seam_cut_total` 708 -> 714) has not landed, and main's budget reads 708. If #2647 lands first, the `seam_cut_total` line in `tests/structure_budgets.json` conflicts. The resolution is main's value less this diff's net -1 (713 if main reads 714), re-measured with `tests/structure.py` at the merged tree, not 707 carried over.

Payments tried, each measured with `tests/structure.py` and `tools/audit/archscore/score.py`:

| payment | seam_cut_total | dS | disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| route-1 alias `currency = self.currency` (round 2) | 709 -> 708 | +0.0000 NULL | withdrawn; review showed a planted alias moves the metric the same way |
| threading `currency` from `_build_data_dict` into `_insight_view`/`_narrative_view` as a parameter | not built | not built | rejected unbuilt: a re-binding of the same read inside one seam, which the brief rules out as a payment |
| `_cop_watch()` in `learning`, shared by `_learning_view` and `_scores_view` | 709 -> 707 | +0.0000 NULL (`--diff 0ebc7cf1e HEAD`) | taken |

The move pays 2: the `views` reads of `_cop_baseline` and `_cop_health_cusum` each counted on both sides of the seam, and the one `views -> learning` call that replaces them counts 2.

| unit | head | what |
|---|---|---|
| U0a gate core | `06c99c0e3` | `tools/ci/ghapi.py` (the one REST client), `prelude.py`, `gate.py` (predicate, `REQUIRED`, `--refresh`, `RATE-LIMITED`), the fixture's additive `gate_required`, the oracle driver `r10_ci_gate_core.py` |

**Assembly.** Conflicts were resolved by keeping every unit's lines:
- `r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py`: each block keeps its own per-file ids, 82 ids with no duplicate. U0a's `rel()` and U9c's `seat_path()` are the same function, so one is kept.
- `tests/layout.json`: `tools/ci/**` appears once.
- `tests/closure.py`: U0b's and U9c's per-file `GATE_FILES` lines and U6-lib's two `INERT` lines are dropped, because U0a's `tools/ci/` prefix classifies those files.
- `closures.json`: a set union.

**Bind** (contract items 2-3):
- `gate.py --sweep` imports `tools/ci/sweep.py` and calls `sweep.main(argv, get, post)` with ghapi's functions. The guarded `FAIL sweep-unavailable` fallback is gone.
- `ghapi.get` takes an optional `headers` argument. This is additive: `get(path, params=None)` still works. `alert_list.bind(get, repo)` prefixes `repos/<repo>/` and forwards the SARIF `Accept` header. Its `__main__` binds `ghapi.get` and fails closed without `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`.
- Under `tools/ci/`, only `ghapi.py` names `urllib`.

**Glue.** Two new `tests/entities.py` pins:
- `gate.REQUIRED`'s sorted union equals the fixture's `gate_required`, which must be sorted and duplicate-free, and `contexts` holds 17.
- The half of the forgery rule that needs no `ci.yml` (DESIGN-P2 2.1): no workflow except `ci.yml` defines a job that can report as `gate`; no workflow or job grants `checks: write` or `write-all`; every workflow declares top-level `permissions:`.

- **ci_probe at this head**: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py ci_probe-1 ci_probe-2 ci_probe-3 ci_probe-4 ci_probe-5 ci_probe-6 ci_probe-7` gave `RESULT survivors=0`, each `KILLED`. ci_probe-5 drops the exact-name test, ci_probe-6 drops review's re-check after the fetch, and ci_probe-7 drops push's check.
- **Seat mutants**: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py`, run at `49ccd4a6c`, gave `RESULT survivors=0`: M0 `0 seat step(s) red`, 101 `KILLED`, no `SURVIVED` and no `NOT RUN` or `PATTERN FOUND` lines, and W1-W3 killed. P2a's ids are `gate-1..3`, `ghapi-1..3`, `prelude-1..2`, `sweep_driver-1..3`, `ruleset_cutover-1..3` and `ci_probe-1..4`. `gate-3` now deletes the bound dispatch; `ghapi-3` deletes the header forwarding.
- **Alert-list mutants**: `sh tools/ci/alert_list_mutants.sh --self-test` refused 9 of 9, including the glue's case "the binding drops the Accept header".
- **Gate predicate**: `r10_ci_gate_core.py mutants`, 16 of 16 killed at U0a's head. The predicate is unchanged here, because the glue touches only `main()`'s `--sweep` arm.
- **Entities pins**: each pin was run against a mutated copy of the tree, through its own block. Dropping `ci-ratchet` from `PUSH_ONLY` gave `only in gate_required: tests / ci-ratchet`. Cutting `contexts` to 16 gave `contexts holds 16`. A `gate` job in `tests.yml` gave `tests.yml: job gate can report as gate`. `checks: write` in `hassfest.yml` gave `top grants checks: write`.

## Null control

- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/selftest_wiring.py --check` reads `87 self-testing, 87 wired, 0 unwired`, rc 0, at the head. At the merge commit before the steps it read `87, 78, 9 unwired`, rc 1.
- `r10_ci_gate_core.py replay --no-b3-fill` gives `rc 1; output DIFFERS`: exactly the two push rows go BAD. `b3 --plant` gives `parity RED`. So the IDENTICAL comparison can fail.
- Each entities pin carries in-file plants: three for the REQUIRED pin and five for the forgery pin. A reader that compares nothing fails its own check.

## Decisions

Confirmed by the orchestrator under mandate 6329234399 (2026-10-22):
1. `ghapi.get(path, params=None, headers=None)`: the `headers` argument is additive, and the contract's two-argument form stands. `alert_list.bind` forwards the SARIF `Accept` header through it.
2. `gate.py --sweep` imports `tools/ci/sweep.py` directly, and the `sweep-unavailable` fallback is removed. Mutant `gate-3` is re-targeted to delete the bound dispatch.
3. alert_list's mutants stay in `tools/ci/alert_list_mutants.sh`, wired as their own `instrument-self-tests` step, and are not duplicated into `r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py`.
4. `tools/audit/seat/tmp_paths.py` gains an `ALLOW` entry for `ci_probe.py`'s self-test fixture, the scratch path its dismissal check must refuse.
5. `tests/closure.py` drops the per-file lines under `tools/ci/` (U0b's and U9c's `GATE_FILES` lines and U6-lib's `INERT` lines), because U0a's `tools/ci/` prefix classifies them.
6. The forgery pin also requires every workflow to declare top-level `permissions:`, so no job falls back to the repository's default token.

7. **Withdrawn.** The `SHARED_GRAMMARS` entry for `[0-9a-f]{40}` is dropped, and `tools/policy/agreement.mjs` is main's bytes. CI's wave-script restores that file from the base (a pinned grader), so the entry could not take effect in this pull request. Split out alone, it reads `DEAD` (see `## Forward-carry`).
8. **Route B.** `ci_probe.py` no longer restates the regex. git owns the SHA shape: `push` and `review` accept a SHA only when `git rev-parse --verify --quiet <sha>^{commit}` prints exactly that SHA, so a short, upper-case or unknown name refuses before any API write. `review` fetches `refs/pull/<pr>/head` first when the commit is not local and refuses if it still is not. `review` has no programmatic caller (`git grep ci_probe` finds only its CLI, workflow step, INSTRUMENTS row and pins). Confirmed under mandate 6329234399.

## Figures

- Self-tests, each `python3 -I <file> --self-test` with the 3.14.7 seat venv:
  - `ghapi` 13 checks, 0 failed;
  - `prelude` 27, 0 failed;
  - `gate` 27, 0 failed;
  - `sweep` 21, 0 failed;
  - `alert_list` 25, 0 failed;
  - `ruleset_cutover` 51, 0 failed;
  - `sweep_driver` 15, 0 failed;
  - `ci_probe` 40, 0 failed (34 before route B: short SHA, upper-case SHA, unknown full SHA before any API write, review fetch-then-refuse, and the two nulls);
  - `python3 tools/audit/seat/prune_refs.py --self-test`: `SELF-TEST PASS (29 checks)`.
- Oracles over the assembled `gate.py`, from `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_ci_gate_core.py`:
  - `replay`: `rc 0; output IDENTICAL to 1371a0a6:measure/rev/gate_replay2.txt`, and `replay --model` reads the same;

- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py`: `4 of 2399 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED` at this head. The same command at `origin/main` a9db47846 reads `4 of 2397 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`, with the same four py-spy heartbeat-control checks. The two new pins read `ok`.
- `python3 tests/structure.py`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`, with no budget raised.
- Other checks:
  - `python3 tests/throwaway_git.py --check`: 0 refused;
  - `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/tmp_paths.py --check`: 0 refused;
  - `ref_privacy.py --check`: 0 refused;

At `19d36dcda` the same base copy gave `UNREGISTERED "[0-9a-f]{40}" in .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs, tools/audit/seat/ci_probe.py`.
- `tools/pr/ci_predict.py --base origin/main`: no closures or fast red predicted.
- `python3 -I tests/harness_headers.py` fails at import here, because `-I` drops `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub`, as U9c reported. The suite's own run is in the gate line below.
- Gate: `PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1 GATE_SCOPE=auto GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=a9db47846647 PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub ./tests/run.sh`, run at `0e066014d` (base a9db478), printed `MODE: FULL`, because `tests/closure.py` and `tools/ci/` are gate files. Result: `4 TEST SCRIPT(S) FAILED` (`optimality.py`, `card.mjs`, `stress.py`, `entities.py`); everything else was `ok`, `harness_headers.py` included (`ALL 109 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`). The #2580 merge since then changed only `cloud_relay.sh`, `INSTRUMENTS.md`, the mutants harness and a delivery row. `entities.py`, `structure.py`, every self-test, the mutants harness and the static checks were re-run at the head. - Line counts, from `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`: 26 files, 3725 insertions, 4 deletions (`governance.yml` +67). Production lines by each unit's own rule (in its body): U0a 450, U0b 317, U6-lib about 140, U9c 309, UP about 310. File totals:
